title: Running Playbooks Safely: Check, Diff, Limit, Tags
intro: A playbook is a repeatable, reviewable recipe for your fleet, and a mistake in it runs on every host at once. Ansible has a dry-run workflow built in. Using it every time is what separates safe automation from fast outages.

steps.prompt: Validate site.yml's syntax against inventory.ini without running anything.
steps.explanation: The YAML and playbook structure parse cleanly.
steps.why: It catches indentation and structure errors in seconds, and belongs in CI on every pull request, together with ansible-lint (servers-tutorial-004).

steps.prompt: See exactly which hosts site.yml would touch.
steps.fake_output:
playbook: site.yml
  play #1 (web): Configure web servers	TAGS: []
    pattern: ['web']
    hosts (3):
      web-01
      web-02
      web-03
steps.why: Before any change, confirm the blast radius. Surprise hosts in this list, like a production group pulled in by a nested inventory, are exactly how the servers-incident-005 accident happened.

steps.prompt: Dry-run the playbook and show the file changes it would make.
steps.fake_output:
TASK [nginx : Deploy nginx.conf] ***
--- before: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
+++ after: /home/alice/.ansible/tmp/nginx.conf
@@ -12,1 +12,1 @@
-    worker_connections 1024;
+    worker_connections 4096;
changed: [web-01]
changed: [web-02]
ok: [web-03]

PLAY RECAP ***
web-01 : ok=6 changed=1 unreachable=0 failed=0
web-02 : ok=6 changed=1 unreachable=0 failed=0
web-03 : ok=6 changed=0 unreachable=0 failed=0
steps.explanation: One config line would change on web-01 and web-02; web-03 is already correct.
steps.why: --check predicts changes without making them, and --diff shows the actual content. This is Ansible's 'terraform plan'. Caveat: tasks that depend on an earlier task's real result (such as installing a package, then configuring it) can't be fully predicted in check mode.

steps.prompt: Apply it to a single canary host first: web-01 only.
steps.fake_output:
RUNNING HANDLER [nginx : reload nginx] ***
changed: [web-01]

PLAY RECAP ***
web-01 : ok=7 changed=2 unreachable=0 failed=0
steps.explanation: The config changed and a handler reloaded nginx, on one host only.
steps.why: --limit narrows any playbook to a subset. Canary first: if the new config breaks something, it breaks one server behind a load balancer, not all of them. Handlers run only when a task reports a change, so nginx isn't reloaded for nothing.

steps.prompt: Later, re-apply only the tasks tagged 'nginx' across the web group.
steps.fake_output:
PLAY RECAP ***
web-01 : ok=3 changed=0 unreachable=0 failed=0
web-02 : ok=3 changed=1 unreachable=0 failed=0
web-03 : ok=3 changed=0 unreachable=0 failed=0
steps.explanation: Only the nginx tasks ran; web-02 was brought in line.
steps.why: Tags let one big site.yml serve many purposes (a full build, or just 'push the nginx config'). A rerun reporting changed=0 on most hosts is the idempotency payoff: running it again is safe, and anything that does change was drift.
